title: Optimizing the Family Firm
coreMove: Keep continuity useful by auditing protected habits harder than ordinary ones and making family-control advantages earn their place.
sourcePressure: Dick Smith and General Cinema show capital allocation discipline inside family-control realities, where continuity can protect patience or shelter weak habits.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Do not romanticize family ownership or attack it; every case must show protection being tested by a scorecard rather than assumed good or bad.

sourceAnchors.name: Dick Smith
sourceAnchors.detail: The source sidecar pairs Chapter 7 with Dick Smith and General Cinema, emphasizing family-control realities and outsider-style capital allocation discipline.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Dick Smith shows that continuity becomes useful only when it still has to answer a hard scorecard.

sourceAnchors.name: General Cinema
sourceAnchors.detail: The source sidecar describes General Cinema as a diversified company associated with Richard A. Smith and a family-linked leadership context.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: General Cinema turns family control into a management test rather than a sentimental backdrop.

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: No more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'.
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: At least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person direct address, retrospective, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human.
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

exampleSpecs.domain: third-generation hotel group deciding whether to keep a beloved banquet hall
exampleSpecs.audience: a family CEO balancing cousins, guests, and renovation capital
exampleSpecs.stakes: the hall consumes maintenance money needed for profitable room upgrades
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Claire compares the banquet hall maintenance ledger with room-upgrade returns and closes weekend banquets while preserving the hotel service standards guests actually value.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: faded banquet carpet curling beside a room-renovation sample board

exampleSpecs.domain: family-owned quarry choosing between ancestral equipment and safer contracted crushing
exampleSpecs.audience: an operations heir whose uncle treats the old crusher as a monument
exampleSpecs.stakes: downtime and safety incidents threatening supply contracts
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Olivier asks his uncle to walk the downtime log line by line, then retires the ancestral crusher because continuity must protect the quarry, not the machine.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: limestone dust settling on an old crusher nameplate

exampleSpecs.domain: independent cinema chain with family ownership and underused weekday screens
exampleSpecs.audience: a programming director whose relatives resist changing old booking rules
exampleSpecs.stakes: weekday losses put two community screens at risk
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: It took Megan one winter attendance report to replace the inherited booking rule with local event rentals that preserve the cinemas by changing how empty screens earn.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a blank marquee reflected in wet pavement

exampleSpecs.domain: family-controlled medical device supplier reviewing protected distributor relationships
exampleSpecs.audience: a commercial lead whose father built the distributor network
exampleSpecs.stakes: hospitals are delaying orders because protected distributors miss service calls
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Henrik overlays service-call delays on the distributor map and cuts the protected account that hurts hospital reliability most.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a sterilized device tray beside a map dotted with missed service calls

exampleSpecs.domain: family-run import warehouse choosing whether to preserve informal credit for longtime retailers
exampleSpecs.audience: a controller who respects the founder's handshake relationships
exampleSpecs.stakes: cash conversion slipping while new suppliers demand faster payment
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: You watch Adaeze sort customer cards by payment days and keep the relationship principle only where it still supports cash discipline and supplier trust.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: index cards with retailer names clipped above a pallet scale

exampleSpecs.domain: family-controlled outdoor gear maker reviewing a legacy product catalog
exampleSpecs.audience: a product head asked to respect the founder's classics
exampleSpecs.stakes: inventory space tied up in slow-moving heritage items while the core tent line sells out
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Which classics are still stewardship and which are insulation? Daniel tags each product by cash, brand pull, and production slot before cutting the protected items that fail all three.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: canvas sample swatches stacked beside a sell-through report

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'

skillTargets: test continuity against capital allocation rather than sentiment
detect insulation created by protected structures
choose optimization over preservation or theatrical disruption
apply owner discipline where relationships make accountability harder

tryThisNowSpec: Name one protected routine and write the scorecard it would have to pass if it had no history attached to it.
